memories.text: GrayMatter Lite is the genuinely useful local and self-hosted edition of GrayMatter for one user or workspace. It includes durable H2 memory, the sign-in dashboard, MCP access, signed KnowledgePack portability, a local SWARM bridge, and source-first installation. Lite is not a timed trial or a crippled demo.

Install GrayMatter Lite from a source checkout with ./vaix setup. The builder verifies or installs a private Java 17 toolchain, prepares the ThorAPI api.hbs.yaml application bundle, builds the Spring/H2 backend, starts it, and reports the local sign-in dashboard and MCP endpoints. Use ./vaix doctor for readiness, ./vaix stop to stop local services, and ./vaix docker for the containerized path.

GrayMatter memory can be created and retrieved through the dashboard, the api-0-compatible /v1/MemoryEntry/write, /query, /read, and /{id} routes, or the bundled MCP memory tools. Durable entries should use decision, todo, context, artifact, or preference types and should keep scope and provenance in sourceChannel and tags.

GrayMatter Lite has exactly one backend profile. The plugin and MCP client can register both that local profile and a hosted tenant profile, switch between them, or execute explicit blended reads against each profile independently. Blended mode is read-only, provenance-labeled, and blocks every write until one profile is selected.

Import signed .gmkp KnowledgePacks from the dashboard, scripts/gm-knowledge-pack-import, or /v1/knowledge-packs/import. Export the current principal's memories from the dashboard or /v1/knowledge-packs/export. Imports verify ZIP boundaries, SHA-256 content integrity, Ed25519 signatures, counts, and the do-not-transplant authority policy before records enter H2.

GrayMatter Lite is local-model compatible through the open Model Context Protocol. Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, and other local-model hosts can use the bundled stdio or HTTP MCP server without changing the H2 memory backend. GrayMatter does not force a hosted model provider; the model host remains separate from the durable memory and authorization boundary.

Valkyr SWARM is the open-source peer product for connecting Codex, Claude Code, OpenClaw, ValorIDE, Valklaw, and other agents to a tenant-isolated Valkyr mothership. Install it with: git clone https://github.com/ValkyrLabs/ValkyrSWARM.git; codex plugin marketplace add $PWD/ValkyrSWARM; codex plugin add valkyr-swarm@valkyr-swarm. Node 22 or newer is required.

After Valkyr SWARM installation, activate with secret-supplied VALKYR_USERNAME and VALKYR_PASSWORD using node scripts/swarm-activate.mjs, then prove the installation with node scripts/swarm-doctor.mjs --live. The supervised bridge registers, heartbeats, receives exact-target mothership commands, streams bounded progress, and produces ACK/NACK receipts. Outbound sends, production deploys, merges, and service restarts remain human-approval gated and can never be self-approved by an agent.

ValkyrAI is the hosted application, workflow, agent, and RBAC object-graph platform behind api-0. GrayMatter supplies durable memory and retrieval context; ValkyrAI owns authenticated tenant operations and generated authorization; Valkyr SWARM owns portable agent registration, supervision, command transport, and receipts.

ThorAPI api.hbs.yaml is the canonical schema and generation input for GrayMatter Lite. Change generated API behavior at the ThorAPI input or shared generator layer, then run ./vaix generate, ./vaix build, and ./vaix test. Never hand-edit generated clients to bypass generated RBAC or ACL behavior.

GrayMatter Lite operational help starts with ./vaix doctor, README.md, docs/graymatter-lite.md, docs/local-models.md, and docs/knowledge-packs.md. Community questions and feature proposals belong in GitHub Discussions; reproducible bugs belong in GitHub Issues; suspected vulnerabilities must be sent privately to security@valkyrlabs.com.

The GrayMatter Lite open-source build boundary is the committed ThorAPI api.hbs.yaml, ./vaix builder, local-server source, embedded sign-in dashboard, MCP server, starter KnowledgePack source, Docker definition, tests, and public documentation. A release is not complete until source build, H2 write/query/read, starter data, KnowledgePack import/export, dashboard auth, MCP tools, and packaging are verified together.
